purpose: Separate stopped, held, mechanically locked, motion-enabled and fault states so commissioning/service procedures and future controls cannot imply access safety from software state alone.

operatorUxRequirements: Never label a software-held zero-speed condition as safe for mechanical access; only SERVICE_LOCKED or an approved equivalent mechanically restrained state permits access under LOTO.
Display or label STOPPED/HELD separately from MECHANICALLY LOCKED.
Provide a directly visible mechanical indication of service-lock engagement; an electrical indicator may supplement but not replace it.
Fault reset is a separate deliberate action and never resumes a previous run/jog command.
Jog controls must visibly indicate restricted commissioning mode and the active reduced motion limits.
A service-index request should show that alignment motion can occur and must not imply the carrier is locked when the index is reached.
Present active fault identity and latched status; where logging is implemented include command, carrier feedback, drive load estimate and stop outcome.
RETENTION_ENGAGED must present an out-of-service condition that cannot be cleared through ordinary operator reset.
Manual release/recovery controls or instructions must state that positive service lock and LOTO precede release of the normal holding path.
Avoid ambiguous colour-only status communication; labels and physical state cues must remain understandable without relying solely on colour.
Do not expose automatic direction reversal as a normal operator option while reversal remains unapproved.
Power restoration must return to a non-moving held/fault state, never silently restore the previous motion command.
manualRecoveryRules: No manual brake/drive release before zero speed and positive service-lock engagement are independently verified.
No recovery procedure may intentionally create uncontrolled free rotation of the 240-element field.
If service-index alignment cannot be achieved under powered controlled motion, a project-specific recovery method must be engineered before access rather than improvising force on the carrier.
Restore the normal holding/braking path and verify it before withdrawing the service lock.
Any retention engagement or structural contact requires engineering disposition before manual movement.
